author: Mark Atwood
text:
Architectural decision deferred to human. Add BackendQueryError<E> { UnsupportedFilter, UnsupportedSort, Other(E) } envelope on JmapBackend::query_objects.

Cost / propagation:
- Trait API change to JmapBackend::query_objects. Every *Backend extension trait (MailBackend, ChatBackend, CalendarsBackend, TasksBackend, ContactsBackend, FileNodeBackend, SharingBackend, MetadataBackend) inherits this via the supertrait, so the change cascades.
- Every implementor (MemoryBackend in each *-server crate + every consumer's production backend) needs to update its return type. ~30 call sites in workspace tests + every future implementor.
- handle_query in crate-jmap-server/src/handlers.rs simplifies: .await.map_err(JmapError::from) instead of the current .map_err(|e| server_fail_from_backend(&e)). One-line win at the handler.

Benefits:
- Backends can emit RFC 8620 §6.4 unsupportedFilter / unsupportedSort as typed errors instead of laundering them through serverFail (which loses spec-level detail and crosses the JMAP-wlip.2 leak surface).
- Symmetry with BackendChangesError shape on get_changes / query_changes.

Costs:
- Same shape as JMAP-wlip.30 / JMAP-wlip.35 — breaking API change to the foundation trait. Belongs paired with the next planned workspace major bump.

Bead author classified P3. The leak path it would close was already mostly closed by JMAP-wlip.2 (server_fail_from_backend strips backend Display text from the wire); this fix would add information rather than remove a security hole.

Decision needed: (a) defer to next major bump, or (b) reshape now and pay the propagation cost.

Recommendation: (a) — pair with JMAP-wlip.30 and JMAP-wlip.35 in a single major-bump propagation pass.
